pricing.notes: Patient-facing healthcare marketplace. NO INSURANCE ACCEPTED - cash pay only. Therapy $75-130/session. Psychiatry $100-175/session (initial up to $350). Mental Health Rx subscription $79/month for ongoing med management. Cannot prescribe controlled substances (no Adderall, benzos, opioids). Patients can submit bills to insurance for reimbursement.

seo.title: Sesame Care: Review & Pricing | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Sesame Care offers affordable cash-pay therapy ($75-130) and psychiatry ($100-175). No insurance accepted. Cannot prescribe controlled substances.

faqs.a: No. Sesame is cash-pay only. You pay upfront and can submit the receipt to your insurance for potential out-of-network reimbursement, but Sesame doesn't bill insurance directly. This keeps prices transparent but means no copay benefits.

faqs.q: How much does therapy cost on Sesame?
faqs.a: $75-130 per session, with most therapists charging around $104. Prices vary by provider and state. You see the exact price before booking. No hidden fees.

faqs.q: How much does psychiatry cost on Sesame?
faqs.a: $100-175 for follow-up visits, but initial psychiatric consultations can run $250-350 depending on location. The $79/month Mental Health Rx subscription is worth considering if you need ongoing medication management.

faqs.q: Can Sesame psychiatrists prescribe Adderall or Xanax?
faqs.a: No. Sesame providers cannot prescribe controlled substances including stimulants (Adderall, Vyvanse, Ritalin), benzodiazepines (Xanax, Klonopin, Ativan, Valium), or opioids. You'll need a different provider for these medications.

faqs.q: What is the Mental Health Rx subscription?
faqs.a: $79/month subscription that includes video visits with a provider, unlimited messaging, and seamless prescription refills for non-controlled medications. Good option if you're stable on SSRIs/SNRIs and just need regular check-ins and refills.

faqs.q: How does Sesame compare to Cerebral or Done?
faqs.a: Sesame is a marketplace (you pick any provider), not a single company. Cerebral and Done specialize in ADHD and can prescribe stimulants—Sesame cannot. Sesame is better for anxiety/depression treatment with non-controlled meds, or general therapy.

faqs.q: Is Sesame good for ADHD treatment?
faqs.a: Only if you don't need stimulant medication. Sesame psychiatrists can prescribe non-stimulant ADHD meds like Strattera or Wellbutrin, but not Adderall, Vyvanse, or Ritalin. For stimulant prescriptions, look at Done, Cerebral, or Talkiatry instead.

one_liner: Cash-pay healthcare marketplace with therapy $75-130/session and psychiatry $100-175. No insurance.
